items.title: Introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway . Virtual Models are an abstraction of the model string and configurations your apps and developers use. With a single virtual model ID, you can change and update models, configure fallbacks and priority, and enforce Zero Data Retention centrally. The virtual model configuration applies wherever the ID is used. Assign a virtual model ID to an agent task, and pass it as the model string wherever that task is called. You can then change the model and settings behind the virtual model ID in AI Gateway, and your apps and agents will pick up the new configuration automatically, without code changes or redeploys. New models use the same virtual model ID In the last 90 days, 125 new models from more than 10 labs became available on AI Gateway. That adds up to about 10 a week. AI Gateway already makes switching a one-line change. You call any of those models by ID, and AI Gateway routes each request to a healthy provider and can fall back to others when one fails. That one line still lives in your code, so switching usually means a redeploy. Virtual Models move model selection and configuration to AI Gateway. You create an ID for a task, like vmc/coding-agent , and then configure the model and the settings it should use: You can then use that virtual model ID as the model string wherever the task runs: For coding agents like Claude Code , Codex , and others, connect them with vercel ai-gateway setup , then select your virtual model in each harness's model picker or configuration. When a different model is available, including one from another provider, edit the virtual model . Every app and agent that calls vmc/coding-agent picks it up within a few minutes, with no code change or deployment needed: Give each task its own model An agent task like support ticket triage can run hundreds of times an hour and needs to be cheap. Other tasks, like legal contract review, may only run a few times a day, but require a high level of reasoning. You can now give each task a purpose-built virtual model and easily evolve that model and configuration over time: Settings such as fallbacks, Zero Data Retention, and tags stay with the virtual model when you switch models. Provider options apply per provider, so an Anthropic-specific setting stops applying when you point the virtual model at an OpenAI model. Review your provider options whenever you switch providers. Before you switch a virtual model that serves production traffic, point a second one, like vmc/coding-agent-candidate , at the new model and run your evals against it. If quality drops after the switch, point the original back at the previous model. Govern which models your team uses and how Anyone on your team can call a virtual model, and team roles control who can make changes to it. Platform and security teams can centrally govern and test models and settings, while still easily giving teams access to new models as they are released. Settings on a virtual model win over the same settings in a request, so callers can't override the provider order, fallbacks, or service tier you chose. For example, you can configure the fallback models for vmc/storefront-assistant centrally, and every app using that virtual model ID will use the same failover configuration, even if a request specifies different fallbacks. If a virtual model requires Zero Data Retention or providers that don't train on request data, those configurations are enforced even if a request explicitly sets zeroDataRetention or disallowPromptTraining to false. Tags on a virtual model replace any tags sent with the request, so spend lands on the task no matter how each app tags its calls. The Virtual Models page shows requests, spend, and success rate for each task. Get started Create a virtual model from your team dashboard or with the Vercel CLI . About AI Gateway AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and doesn't charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. Virtual Models work with every model type on AI Gateway, including image, video, speech, embedding, and realtime models, and with the AI SDK and the OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs. See the Virtual Models documentation for every setting. Read more

items.title: The spyware hiding in old script tags
items.summary: 🚀 Frontend Focus #​764 — October 28, 2026 | Read on the web 🖼️ HTML-in-Canvas: Interactive DOM Inside 2D, WebGL and WebGPU Canvases — Arriving in stable Chrome next week, this long-incubated API draws real, live HTML into 2D, WebGL and WebGPU canvases, with text selection, form controls, Find-in-Page and screen readers all still working. Three.js, Babylon.js and PixiJS already support it. Chrome-only for now, but a big leap for canvas-heavy UIs. There's a related video here too . Natalia Markoborodova (Chrome) Creating Dynamic Social Media Cards for User Content — Chris digs into how links unfurl across Discord, X, Slack, Bluesky, iMessage and more, and argues most dynamic social cards waste the image by just restating the title and description. Then he shows what should go on it instead. Chris Coyier Would You Let Your AI Agent Grade Its Own Homework? — Agents write code faster than ever. They even review their own work. But who’s reviewing them? Dropbox, Notion & ElevenLabs don’t take the risk. With Meticulous, every change is exhaustively verified, with zero developer effort. Meticulous sponsor DeadTag: Forgotten Third-Party Script Tags Became a Delivery Network for Spyware — Attackers are buying up expired domains once used by analytics, ad and widget scripts, so any site still carrying the old tag now silently loads attacker code. A worthy reminder to go audit those tags! Scott Helme ⚡️ IN BRIEF 🎉 CSS-Tricks , after a spell under the ownership of DigitalOcean, is independent once again under the stewardship of editor Geoff Graham . 🦊 Firefox 159 enables scroll-driven animations by default, so they now work in all major engines. It also adds scoped custom element registries. 🪪 Since Chrome 155, sites can use the Digital Credentials API to offer credentials , such as digital IDs, to a compatible wallet app on the user's phone. ⚙️ W3C has launched a polyfill pilot for WebMCP , a JavaScript API that exposes web app functionality as agent-callable tools. 🌅 The Arc browser is being sunset this December, and Dia is suggested as a viable alternative. Zen is another, non-Chromium variant. 📺 Firefox has ▶️ a new ad with various 'meme icons' from years gone by (Numa Numa Guy kicks things off). 📙 Articles, Opinions & Tutorials WebKit Features for Safari 27.1 — A fresh release of Safari came out alongside Apple's new foldable. There's advice on how to create layouts for folding screens using Device Posture API and the Viewport Segments API . Both are behind feature flags for now. Jen Simmons (WebKit) 💡 Safari 27.2 followed days later , adding ::field-content for styling a customizable select's displayed text, and renaming Grid Lanes' flow-tolerance to fit-tolerance . Investigating a Curious Case of Font Format Fallbacks — Paul chases a bug in which a site's font loaded three times in a row , as WOFF2, then WOFF, then TTF, following the browser's error messages into Chromium's own source to find the cause. Paul Calvano 🗓️ Workshop: How to Implement Session Replay — Filters, custom tags, and sampling settings for finding the sessions that matter. Nov 5, 10am PT. Sentry sponsor Performance Budgets Need a Representative Worst — Harry revises his own long-standing advice: a budget set from your single worst result lets one outlier hide real regressions, so start from a representative worst (P90 or P95 of recent data) instead. A spreadsheet template is included. Harry Roberts ▶ The Most Vulnerable Week in Internet History — A fast recap of a rough security week: PHP2Shell (a pair of PHP engine bugs allowing unauthenticated RCE), a backdoored LiteLLM release, a CA with private keys that were numbers under 256, and more. Fireship Building an Isolated Preview for AI-Generated HTML — Any app that lets a model generate UI has to render the HTML it hands back. Keshav builds five demos showing how a preview can be attacked, then hardens it with iframe sandboxing, CSP and a carefully checked postMessage handler. Keshav Malik 🖨️ Websites Should Be Printable — Brennen printed his own site, didn't like the result, and walks through the print stylesheet changes that fixed it: a hidden header, 12pt type, and black links. Brennen Puth ▶ Why I'm Still Making CSS Tutorials — On caring about the craft of little details and why they matter in an age of agentic code generation. Kevin Powell 🧰 Tools, Code & Resources TitleArt: Make Text Like It's 1997 — Aww yeah, a big dose of nostalgia for users of Microsoft Office back in the 90s. Every classic WordArt style, shape and 3-D effect recreated in the browser. Davey Barker The “Last 90 Days” Filter Shouldn’t Need a Spinner — Bigger date ranges mean your chart’s query scans more rows. TimescaleDB keeps it fast in Postgres. Get $1000 credit . Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor The Website Specification: Every Technical Detail a Site Needs Before Launch — A checklist you (or an agent) can work through before launch, covering SEO, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, i18n, and more. Joost de Valk browser-whisper 2.0: In-Browser Audio and Video Transcription with WebGPU — A library that runs Whisper, Moonshine and other speech models entirely in the browser over WebGPU (with a WASM fallback), complete with timestamped segments, cached models and live mic input. Tanpreet Singh Jolly 🔊 UI SFX: A Library of 930+ Interface Sound Effects — 78 UI sound cues (clicks, toggles, success, add-to-cart, loading loops…) in 12 swappable styles, from minimal to arcade. A ~12KB runtime synthesizes them with Web Audio, or use the 936 CC0 MP3/Ogg files. Source code . Romain Simon MicroKit: 54 Copy-Paste React Microinteractions, CSS-First — Free animated buttons, hover effects, tabs and inputs, each available in TS or JS and in plain CSS or Tailwind. About half need no dependencies, and they're the sort of little details that lift a UI. Henrique Barone 📰 Classifieds 📮 CraftForms : Hosted forms for any site, no backend needed. Two-line embed, unlimited submissions even on the free plan , no captcha. 🧾 Add PDF editing to your app with Foxit's API : Merge, split, rotate, replace pages and flatten annotations, with working code. 🌿 ...and finally Overgrown: When Plants Invade Your Abandoned Tabs — Leave a tab unread too long and this Chrome extension has vines grow across it, until you work your way back in with a machete, chainsaw or flamethrower(!). items.title: Run Paseo agents on Vercel Sandbox
items.summary: Paseo now supports running fx, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Pi in the cloud with the Vercel Sandbox plugin . You can now start an agent in Vercel Sandbox from Paseo on your laptop, then connect from your phone to control the same session, even when your laptop is closed. Stopping a sandbox saves your files and conversation history so you can pick up where you left off. Active processes stop with the sandbox. Enter your Vercel AI Gateway key once during setup. The plugin reuses it for model requests across your sessions, keeping the key outside the sandbox. To get started, enable plugins in Settings → Plugins in Paseo. items.title: Particle-1 is now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Particle-1 from Particle AI is now available on AI Gateway . It is post-trained on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, with a focus on completing software engineering tasks using fewer tokens. Particle describes the gains as shorter reasoning, fewer rounds of trial and repair, and more focused exploration. Use it for debugging, planning code changes, and breaking down multi-step engineering problems. Particle-1 has a 1M-token context window for working with code and extended task histories. Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in your environment. Use particle/particle-1 as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest version of Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select particle/particle-1 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Particle-1 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

items.title: The fx adapter now runs the harness on the host
items.summary: The fx adapter for the AI SDK’s HarnessAgent now runs the harness and model requests in the same process as your application. Built-in filesystem and shell operations remain isolated in the sandbox. The adapter uses libfx , the TypeScript library for fx. It no longer needs to install fx inside the sandbox, run a sandbox bridge, or expose a sandbox port. Model credentials stay on the host rather than being forwarded into the sandbox. The rewrite also adds: Built-in tool filtering: choose which built-in tools the agent can use Mid-turn steering: send new instructions while a turn is running Structured output: generate responses that match a schema Image tool results: return images to the model through toModelOutput() Sessions can be saved and resumed in a new host process. items.title: Vercel Sandbox commands now support stdin
items.summary: Vercel Sandbox now lets you send input to running commands through standard input (stdin). Use it to exchange messages with stdio MCP servers such as agent-browser , or send data to other command-line programs while they run. In the TypeScript SDK, set stdin: true and detached: true in runCommand() . Use writeStdin() to send input and closeStdin() when you’re done: You can also set stdin to a Node.js readable stream, such as process.stdin . The SDK forwards the stream’s data and closes the command’s standard input when the stream ends. In the Python SDK, set stdin=subprocess.PIPE and send input with server.stdin.send() . Call communicate() to close stdin, collect remaining output, and wait for the process to exit: For commands that receive all their input at once, you can pass input directly to Python’s run_process() . items.summaryJa: プロパティの追加・更新は同じ書き方で行い、既存キーには上書きされ、存在しないキーは新規追加になる。 delete を使ってキーごと消去でき、削除後はそのキーを読むと undefined になるが、undefined を代入する別の書き方とは異なる。 ブラケット記法は、キーを変数で指定したい場合や、キー名にスペース・ハイフンが含まれる場合に有効で、ドット記法と使い分けるべき場面がある。

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra from OpenAI is now available on AI Gateway . GPT-6.1 Terra is a fast model for visual reasoning, computer use, and writing, and it improves on the previous Terra model in visual reasoning, factual accuracy, and coding. It suits high-volume work in documents and desktop apps, such as filling out forms, interpreting technical drawings, or entering invoice details into accounting software. OpenAI still recommends its larger GPT-6 models for the most complex coding tasks. The model accepts text and images and returns text, with a context window of more than 1M tokens. It supports configurable reasoning effort , structured outputs , tool calling, and implicit and explicit prompt caching . For latency-sensitive work, fast mode is available as openai/gpt-6.1-terra-fast . GPT-6.1 Terra works with the AI SDK , the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API , the Responses API , and coding agents connected to AI Gateway. Use openai/gpt-6.1-terra as the model name: To use it in Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select openai/gpt-6.1-terra in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try GPT-6.1 Terra in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. items.titleJa: Figmaの用語はほぼCSSに対応していた。読めるが作れなかったコーダーの入り口
items.summaryJa: Figmaの用語はほぼCSSに対応しており、読み取りはできても自分で作る段階には至っていなかった筆者が、ラフ作成の過程で覚えるべき用語を整理することで、動画視聴の動機を失うレベルに理解を深めた。 実際にはフレームやレイアウト、コンポーネント、変数などの概念と名称を対応づけ、Auto Layoutやグリッドの新機能もCSSの知識と結びつけて整理した結果、ラフ作成では4つの機能（フレーム、矩形、テキスト、整列）だけを使うにとどまった。 それにより、読解と作成のギャップは「用語の差異を埋めること」で解消され、用語の理解が進むほど動画の必要性が薄れた。
